chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at what age a child is taken for fasting, so he said: 'Between fifteen and fourteen years, and if he fasts before that, let him be.'
ai.seo_question: At what age does a Shia child become legally responsible for fasting?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the onset of fasting obligation (bulugh) for children occurs between the ages of fourteen and fifteen, a range reflecting the gradual transition to legal responsibility in Shia fiqh. The instruction to allow pre-pubertal fasting without compulsion highlights the pedagogical approach of encouraging voluntary worship to build habit and spiritual discipline before the fast becomes strictly binding.
